headline: The model stops cheating: PLAICRAFT v2 learns when to swing
lede: The scoring audit caught the trained net reading a copy of its own exam answer — a feature that was bit-identical to the swing-intent label. It's gone: v2 infers distance from monster bearing and range, and the perfect 100% intent score became an honest 98.6%.

notes.text: monReach dropped from the seat's senses (32→31); arch 31-24-24-5, stamp plaicraft-bc/v2; full corpus regenerated — 221,418 rows, every recording replay-verified.

Held-out score once, same discipline: still 8/8 wins, average score 155,487 vs v1's 121,306 — fewer cheat flags, better play. Teacher-forcing intent fell to 0.986, which is the point: that's learning now.

New plaicraftcheck gate forbids any input column equal to the label (proven red twice); the trainer refuses stale-width datasets; the attract ticker's held-out claim now reads the shipped weights' own record so no retrain can strand a stale 8/8.

The research page finally serves what the trainer writes — public/research/results.json had drifted since launch and displayed the leaked 100%. It now carries v2's honest numbers plus a note explaining what v1's 100% really was.

look.text: Watch the trained net play the attract demo — seat 2 is all inference now
